subject: Post-call deep-dive: throughput & latency constraints, model topology for Clearwater Labs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@clearwaterlabs.com>, Samira Khoury <samira@clearwaterlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap and requested inputs (Clearwater labs)

Alex / Samira — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of the items we discussed and the inputs we need to size a realistic deployment and SLO proposal: 

1) Key pain points you reiterated:
- User-facing generation latency spiking during batch promotions (current p95 ~ 600ms for short prompts).
- Cost unpredictability when nightly analytics jobs run concurrently with production traffic.
- Need for graceful degradation (keep core assistant online during peak).

2) Goals you described:
- End-user 95th/99th percentile latency target: 150ms p95 for 128-token interactive requests; goal p99 < 300ms for same profile.
- Predictable monthly inference spend (budgeting for Q2 pilot + production).
- SOC2-aligned network boundaries and audit logs.

3) Data points we asked for (please attach if available):
- Estimated traffic profile: peak QPS, average QPS, concurrency at peak.
- Token length distribution (p50/p90 for both prompts and responses).
- Fraction of requests that are embeddings vs generation vs 1-shot/chain-of-thought.
- Any blocked model families (e.g., cannot use non-open models).

4) Initial topology notes from call (high-level):
- Likely approach: small dedicated GPU pool for steady-state + burst capacity into hosted pool.
- Prefetch/KV caching on common prefixes + response caching for short prompts.
- Model variants: 8-bit quantized 13B as primary, 7B fallback for high load.

Attachments: capacity-estimates.xlsx (blank template we mentioned), call-recording-20280320.mp3

Requested next steps: 
- Alex: please send the traffic CSV and token distro by EOD Friday so we can run capacity sims.
- We (Redwood): produce two topology proposals (Dedicated-first and Hybrid-fallback) and an initial cost range by next Tuesday.
- Schedule a 45-minute follow-up deep-dive to land SLOs and rollout plan (propose Mon/Wed next week).

If I missed anything important, tell me now — otherwise we’ll draft the topology options and a concrete mutual action plan.

Best,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0147

--
Attachment: capacity-estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: call-recording-20280320.mp3 (audio stub)
From: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@clearwaterlabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samira Khoury <samira@clearwaterlabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and requested inputs (Clearwater labs)

Thanks Connor — great summary. Two quick clarifications and the first batch of numbers below. I’ll attach the CSV in a second email but wanted these in-line for your sims: 

Traffic (US production region):
- Peak sustained QPS: 120
- Peak concurrency (short window): ~420 concurrent streams
- Average QPS: ~28

Token distribution (approx):
- 0–64 tokens: 78%
- 65–256 tokens: 17%
- >256 tokens: 5%

Workload mix:
- Generation (assistant/chat): 82%
- Embeddings: 12%
- Reranking/batch offline jobs: 6% (typically run midnight–3am)

Model constraints:
- We prefer open weights where possible (we have internal procurement friction for closed-source hosted-only models).
- Quantization is fine as long as quality delta is within our acceptance tests (we’ll share evaluation prompts).

Compliance:
- SOC2 Type II required before production rollout. Data residency US-east for audit logs.

Timeline / Pilot:
- Interested in a 6-week PoC starting mid-April with a 6-week evaluation period.
- Budget band for pilot: $20k–$35k for the period (flexible depending on performance).

I’ll upload the traffic CSV + a small sample of prompts later today. Let us know if any of these numbers change your initial approach.

—Alex
Alex Tucker
Director, Platform Engineering
Clearwater Labs
alex.tucker@clearwaterlabs.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@clearwaterlabs.com>, Samira Khoury <samira@clearwaterlabs.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed topology options & what we’ll simulate next

Alex / team — thanks for the numbers; that traffic profile is very helpful. High-level choices we’ll simulate and the key assumptions we’ll vary: 

Option A — Dedicated-primary (preferred for strict SLOs):
- 6x A100-equivalent instances in a dedicated pool sized for steady-state (~30–40 QPS sustained at p95 target) and an autoscaler that adds 2 instances per 60s when queue depth grows.
- Continuous batching with dynamic sequence packing for short requests (target batch sizes tuned to keep p95 under 150ms).
- KV cache for repeated prefixes (expected to reduce tokens by ~12% for your dataset).
- Fallback: route to quantized 7B (lower cost, slightly higher latency) when queue depth exceeds threshold or when billing alerts trip.

Option B — Hybrid routing with hosted burst: 
- Smaller dedicated pool (3x instances) sized to absorb baseline and most spikes. 
- Burst to Redwood hosted fleet for overflow (model parity via pre-validated quantization profiles).
- This reduces reserved spend but introduces cold-fallback network hops — we’ll model the tail latency impact.

Simulation variables we’ll run: token-length distributions you provided, 80/20 short/long split, embedding windows, and a night-batch concurrency scenario. For each run we’ll output: p50/p95/p99 latency by model variant, estimated token-unit cost, and expected monthly bill for pilot vs prod.

Security/compliance notes:
- We’ll keep control plane interactions routed through your VPC (if you choose Private) and produce an audit-log sampling plan for SOC2 evidence.

Deliverables and timeline (tentative):
- Tue (Mar 26): Sim results + two topology PDFs + cost bands.
- Thu (Mar 28): Draft mutual action plan + PoC steps and checklist.

One ask: please confirm whether you want model families restricted to open-source only for the pilot (we can include a hosted-closed model as a comparison but procurement said that’s a blocker).

I’ll schedule the 45-minute follow-up for Tue/Wed next week — what time window works best for you?

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@clearwaterlabs.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed topology options & what we’ll simulate next

Alex — happy to jump on the follow-up. Quick note on cost posture so expectations align heading into the sims: 

- For Option A (Dedicated-primary) we’ll model a reserved commitment for the pilot with a typical uplift to account for peak chassis (estimate: $22k–$30k for the 6-week pilot depending on exact instance mix).
- For Option B (Hybrid), expected pilot spend can land lower ($14k–$20k) but production costs depend heavily on burst frequency — we’ll show sensitivity curves.

I’ll include a short pricing appendix with the simulation deliverable. Connor will share the meeting invite after Alex confirms availability.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
